title: Contributor Onboarding and Lint Pipeline for Docs Site
author: Maya Torres
content:
Overview:
This playbook documents the recommended contributor onboarding flow for the Docs Site repository, plus the continuous integration (CI) lint pipeline and local checks every contributor should run before submitting a PR. The goal is to reduce authoring friction, lower review cycles, and keep the docs site fast and correct for customers.

Who this is for:
- New documentation contributors (engineers, product, and technical writers)
- Maintainers and reviewers of the docs-site repo
- Developer experience (DevX) and DX tools engineers

High-level goals:
1) Make new contributors productive in < 2 hours.
2) Block common formatting, link, and snippet regressions at CI time.
3) Provide a reproducible local pre-commit checklist for fast feedback.

Ownership and contact:
- Maintainers: eng-developer-experience/docs-site team (primary contact: @maya.torres)
- CI pipeline owner: @ravi.patel (DevX infra)
- Escalation: docs-site-maintainers Slack channel (#docs-site)

Quickstart: first PR in 6 steps
1. Fork the repo: git clone git@github.com:redwood-inference/docs-site.git && cd docs-site
2. Bootstrap local environment: ./scripts/bootstrap.sh (see Appendix A for expected dependencies)
3. Run the pre-commit hooks: pre-commit run --all-files
4. Create a feature branch: git checkout -b fix/snippet-typo-<issue#>
5. Make edits and run local checks: ./scripts/check-all.sh
6. Push and open PR using the docs PR template: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs-site/.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md

Pipeline overview (what CI enforces)
- Stage: lint-format
  - Tools: prettier, markdownlint, remark-lint (config in .remarkrc)
  - Checks: trailing whitespace, heading levels, line length exceptions, consistent code fence languages
- Stage: links-and-assets
  - Tools: htmlproofer (site build mode), custom link-checker
  - Checks: broken internal links, missing image assets, mismatched anchors across versions
- Stage: code-snippet-validate
  - Tools: snippet-runner (internal), node/python/ruby matrix where applicable
  - Checks: snippet executes without syntax errors, examples return expected JSON shapes for API samples
- Stage: accessibility-scan
  - Tools: axe-core CLI run against built static site
  - Checks: ARIA violations, missing alt text on images, color contrast failures above threshold
- Stage: preview-deploy
  - Tools: ephemeral Netlify preview (or internal preview runner)
  - Checks: preview URL available and linked in PR for reviewer QA

Pre-commit and local developer checklist (recommended)
- Required local dependencies: Node 18+, pnpm, Python 3.10+, Hugo 0.111.x (if using Hugo build), Docker (optional for snippet isolation)
- Run sequence:
  1. pnpm install
  2. pnpm build:lint (runs prettier and remark)
  3. pnpm run link-check (fast link scanner for staged files)
  4. ./scripts/snippet-validate.sh <changed-files>
  5. git add . && pre-commit run --all-files

Branching, releases, and versioned docs
- Main branch policy: main always deployable. No direct pushes to main—use PRs.
- Release branches: release/x.y are created for major product releases and get cherry-picks for urgent docs fixes.
- Versioned site handling: we maintain a version map in /content/versions.yaml. When a new model or API surface is released, create a new entry using the versioning checklist in Appendix B.

Reviewer checklist (PR review guide)
- Sanity and scope: Does the PR address only what it claims? Are there unrelated formatting-only changes?
- Accuracy: Verify API examples match latest SDK signatures (see API examples binder in /examples/)
- Build and preview: Confirm preview link builds and pages render correctly
- Accessibility: Spot-check for missing alt text and semantic headings
- Localization flags: If content will be localized, add the label "i18n-ready" and a notes block describing translatable strings

Failure modes and common fixes
- Broken snippet when run in CI: See snippet-runner logs under artifacts. Common fixes: pin interpreter versions in snippet shebang, add missing environment variables to /scripts/snippet-env.example, or add a guarded mock response for network calls.
- Internal link broken only in versioned builds: Verify anchor naming; run pnpm run link-check --matrix to test against built version directories.
- Lint rule false positive for complex tables: Use <!-- lint-disable:rule-name --> comment sparingly and include reviewer justification in PR description.

Templates and examples (locations)
- PR template: .github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md
- Docs front-matter template: /docs/templates/front-matter.md
- API example harness: /examples/api-playground/README.md

Appendix A — Local bootstrap steps
1. Install Node 18+ and pnpm: curl -fsSL https://get.pnpm.io/install.sh | sh
2. Clone repo and run bootstrap: git clone git@github.com:redwood-inference/docs-site.git && cd docs-site && ./scripts/bootstrap.sh
3. Expected output from bootstrap: node_modules installed, pre-commit configured, local dev server available at http://localhost:3000

Appendix B — Versioning checklist (for new product/API releases)
- Create release/x.y branch from main
- Add entry to content/versions.yaml with: version, date, change-log link
- Update API example matrix in /examples/api-playground/matrix.yaml to include the new model/SDK mapping
- Run pnpm run build:versioned to validate redirects and older anchors

Security and credentials guidance
- Never commit live API keys or customer data; use placeholders in examples and .env.example files.
- For runnable snippets that require auth, use a mocked credentials provider and document how to replace with a test key stored in the contributor's local .env (never in the repo).

Migration notes for maintainers (operational runbook)
- When upgrading the lint toolchain, create a compatibility branch and run the full CI matrix for two weeks before merging to main.
- If htmlproofer finds recurrent false positives for external partners, add a suppressed-external-links list that lives in /config/external-links-ignore.txt and is reviewed quarterly.

Glossary and abbreviations
- DevX: Developer Experience
- CI: Continuous Integration
- PR: Pull Request
- ARIA: Accessible Rich Internet Applications

Change log
- 2026-01-15: Initial draft and onboarding steps (Maya Torres)
- 2026-02-20: Added CI stage details, snippet-runner guidance, and accessibility checks (Ravi Patel, Elena Gomez)

End of document
